summary: The worst week on this account, and it did not happen because ALTR went quiet — this week ALTR was faster than it has been in six weeks. It happened because outcomes finally caught up. On Sep 14 Barbara issued the first explicit retention warning of the relationship, unprompted, off her own numbers: 'i really want to continue working together, i just need to see some changes because where the numbers are right now isn’t sustainable for me.' She asked for one specific thing in that message — that @fonta prioritise recovering the accounts sitting in limbo — and named the outcome she wanted: 'i’d love to figure out a clear plan for what we can do to start getting things moving back in the right direction.' Mayson answered in 38 minutes with 'Let’s hop on a call tomorrow @barbsilvaxo and go over it!' and there is no evidence anywhere in the chat that the call happened, no plan was posted, and the numbers question was never answered. What she got instead on Sep 16 was a new ask — 'do you have a facebook account available to use?' — a brand new workstream opened two days after she said the current ones are not sustainable. Then on Sep 17 at 15:10 her MAIN account went down: 'SOS', 'CAN SOMEONE PLEASE HELP ME', 'I AM FREAKING OUT', '@ofwizz u think im cooked'. @thebrazilianfitbarbie — the asset every other workstream on this account feeds — is now gone alongside the two secondaries that have been gone since August. Derrek re-entered the chat for the first time in 36 days and responded in six minutes, Olivia pivoted to what is controllable inside 14 minutes, and Vivek managed 'Strange'. The chat then goes silent from Sep 17 15:46 to window close — she was left overnight, seventeen hours, after 'I AM FREAKING OUT', with no status. Meanwhile Vivek's account-recovery promise broke for the second time: 'Will do tomorrow' (Sep 10, due Sep 11) became 'Will do it today' (Sep 15) and nothing has been reported in 8 days. Billing had a genuinely good week and then a bad one: the day-before heads-up was restored (Sep 14), the invoice landed on cadence (Sep 15), Barbara paid inside 20 hours — and on Sep 16 Stephski disclosed she had under-invoiced by 143%, 'the total shouldve been 2,859.72 based on that math not $1176.60', leaving $1,683.12 outstanding at window close. And Michelle's weekly leak-removal report — the one service Barbara thanks ALTR for every single week, six weeks running — did not go out. Michelle sent zero messages in the entire window, in the exact week the client said she is considering leaving.

health.rationale: Down 13 from 55 (2026-09-11), the steepest single-window drop on the account and the lowest score recorded. This is not a responsiveness failure — responsiveness was the best it has been since July. Mayson replied to the retention warning in 38 minutes; Derrek broke a 36-day silence and answered the emergency in 6 minutes; Olivia was constructive within 14 minutes; Stephski restored the heads-up, sent on cadence, and self-disclosed her own invoicing error; Mica held her inspo cadence a second consecutive week and pushed a proactive Instagram security bulletin. The score collapses on outcomes and on what the client said out loud. (1) She wrote a churn sentence on Sep 14: 'where the numbers are right now isn’t sustainable for me.' Nobody has answered the numbers question and there is no evidence the call Mayson offered for Sep 15 was ever held. (2) Her main account @thebrazilianfitbarbie was banned Sep 17 — the two secondaries have been gone since August, so she now has no working Instagram at all, 46 days after she first raised account flagging and 60 days after onboarding without ever being shown a single posting, view or growth number. (3) Vivek broke the same recovery promise twice in six days and contributed three words of substance all window. (4) ALTR asked for $1,683.12 more after she had already paid, off a 143% invoicing error. (5) The single most trusted service on the account — Michelle's weekly leak report — silently stopped in the worst possible week. (6) The pausing-of-work clause was repeated on the Sep 15 invoice, so it is now policy rather than a one-off, aimed at a client who is four-for-four on paying in full. Held above 40 only by Derrek's return, Olivia's Sep 17 handling and Mica's restored cadence.
